title: Compute surface energy coefficients σ⁰, σ¹ and μ¹ for alkali metals
action:
Implement the variational surface energy model: For each metal (Cs, Rb, K, Na, Li) use its bulk electron density n+ (in a.u.) given below:
  Cs: 1.33e-3, Rb: 1.67e-3, K: 1.95e-3, Na: 3.77e-3, Li: 6.92e-3.
  The planar surface energy σ⁰(b) is expressed as
  σ⁰ = C_g^0 n+ b⁻³ − C_t^0 n+^{5/3} b⁻¹ + C_ex^0 n+^{4/3} b⁻¹ + C_c^0 n+ b⁻¹ + C_g^0 n+ b,
  with zeroth-order coefficients:
  C_g^0 = 3.768, C_t^0 = 2.184, C_ex^0 = 0.329, C_c^0 = 0.008556.
  The first-order curvature correction σ¹(b) has the same functional form (substitute j=1 coefficients) and is evaluated at b=b⁰:
  σ¹(b) = C_g^1 n+ b⁻³ − C_t^1 n+^{5/3} b⁻¹ + C_ex^1 n+^{4/3} b⁻¹ + C_c^1 n+ b⁻¹ + C_g^1 n+ b,
  with C_g^1 = 0, C_t^1 = 0.824, C_ex^1 = 0.275, C_c^1 = 0.01621.
  Solve dσ⁰/db = 0 to obtain b⁰ (the biquadratic equation reduces to a quadratic in b²; take the positive root). Then compute b¹, the first-order perturbation of the optimal thickness, using the formula derived from the variational condition:
  b¹ = - (∂σ¹/∂b) / (∂²σ⁰/∂b²) evaluated at b = b⁰.
  Compute σ¹ by evaluating σ¹(b⁰).
  Compute the chemical potential correction μ¹ using:
  Δφ = 2π³ n+ / (3 b⁰³),
  μ¹ = -Δφ (1/2 + b¹/b⁰) - 2 σ⁰ b⁰ / n+ + (b⁰)² / 72.
  Output the results as a CSV with columns metal, n_plus, b0, b1, sigma0, sigma1, mu1.
description: CSV containing the computed planar surface energy σ⁰, first-order curvature correction σ¹, optimal surface-layer inverse thickness b⁰ and its first-order correction b¹, and chemical potential correction μ¹ for Cs, Rb, K, Na, Li. All values in atomic units.
output_schema: Columns: metal (string), n_plus (float, a.u.), b0 (float, a.u.), b1 (float, a.u.), sigma0 (float, a.u.), sigma1 (float, a.u.), mu1 (float, a.u.). One row per metal.

title: Compute critical charge Z* for positively charged sodium particles
action: Using the ion work function for Na (W+ = 3.7 eV, as provided in the instruction), convert to atomic units. For ionic radii R from 5 to 30 a₀ in steps of 1 a₀, compute the critical charge Z* = W+ * R + 1/2. Output a CSV with columns R and Z_star.
description: CSV containing the critical charge Z* at which a positively charged sodium particle becomes unstable against Coulomb explosion, as a function of ionic radius R.
output_schema: Columns: R (float, a.u.), Z_star (float, dimensionless). R from 5.0 to 30.0 in steps of 1.0. Z_star computed as W+ * R + 0.5.
